status_summary: As of 2026-10-15 the NRC has finalized several streamlining rules, while the Mandate's ALARA replacement and codified review deadlines are not final. Executive Order 14300 (2025-05-23) set maximum decision periods of 18 months for new reactor applications and 12 months for continued operation, fixed caps on hourly fee recovery, reconsideration of the linear no-threshold model and ALARA, and final rules within 18 months. Final rules include a 40-year design certification duration (confirmed effective 2025-09-15), the advanced reactor framework and categorical exclusions from environmental review (both 2026-03-30; the NRC says the exclusions rulemaking began before the order), codified generic environmental findings for new reactors (2026-04-24) and FY2026 fees with fixed service-fee caps (2026-06-16, caps effective 2026-10-01); a direct final rule modernizing NRC rulemaking procedures under the order was published 2026-08-11, with its effective date confirmed as 2026-10-26. The FY2026 fee rule states that the 12 and 18 month decision deadlines will be addressed in a future rulemaking, and the ALARA proposal (2026-07-15), the NEPA implementation proposal (2026-07-07) and the reactor licensing and siting proposal (2026-07-16) are not final. A trade report of 2026-05-20 counted five of 27 planned rulemakings as final and said the NRC chair conceded some final rules would follow the order's target of about 2026-11-23. Since then the NRC has published a proposal on reactor licensing, decommissioning and operational oversight (2026-09-24) and two direct final rules that take effect only if no significant adverse comment arrives: expanded exemptions from materials licensing (published 2026-10-05, effective 2026-12-21) and a 40-year renewal of the AP1000 design certification (published 2026-10-14, effective 2026-12-28).

timeline.event: Executive Order 14300 directs the NRC to decide new reactor applications within 18 months and continued-operation applications within 12 months, to set fixed caps on hourly fee recovery, to reconsider reliance on the linear no-threshold model and ALARA, and to issue proposed rules within 9 months and final rules within 18 months.
NRC confirms the 2025-09-15 effective date of its direct final rule (published 2025-07-02) extending design certification duration from 15 to 40 years.
NRC publishes a final rule adding a risk-informed, technology-inclusive licensing framework for commercial nuclear plants, including advanced reactors that do not use light-water technology.

NRC publishes a final rule on categorical exclusions from environmental review (effective 2026-04-29); the NRC says the rulemaking was under way before Executive Order 14300 and that expanding exclusions for new reactor licensing was outside the rule's scope.
NRC publishes a rule codifying generic environmental findings for licensing new nuclear reactors.

POWER Magazine reports the NRC has finalized 5 of 27 planned rulemakings tied to the order, that the chair conceded some final rules will come after the 18-month target, and that ALARA and linear no-threshold reconsideration was still in development.

NRC publishes its FY2026 fee rule (effective 2026-08-17) with fixed caps on service fees under Executive Order 14300 section 5(a), effective 2026-10-01, and states the 12 and 18 month decision deadlines will be addressed in a future rulemaking; about 818.8 million of 971.5 million dollars in budget authority is targeted for fee recovery.

NRC publishes a proposed rule on implementing the National Environmental Policy Act that narrows the scope of NEPA review, updates review procedures and categorical exclusions, and issues draft guidance.

NRC publishes the radiation protection proposal: it would remove the term ALARA from regulations and guidance in favor of a graded approach to dose management, keep current dose limits, and retain the linear dose-response model as a partial basis. Comments due 2026-08-31.

NRC publishes a proposal modernizing reactor licensing, oversight and siting under 10 CFR Parts 50, 52 and 53 (earlier construction start, no expiration for early site permits, risk-informed alternatives, revised design-change thresholds and a two-tier siting approach). Comments due 2026-08-31.

NRC publishes a proposed rule, Regulatory Enhancements for Reactor Licensing, Decommissioning, and Operational Oversight, described in its abstract as part of the overhaul under Executive Order 14300 (read as a listing abstract only).

NRC publishes a direct final rule, Exemptions From Materials Licensing (91 FR 63133), described as deregulatory and citing Executive Order 14300; effective 2026-12-21 unless significant adverse comments arrive by 2026-11-04, with a companion proposed rule the same day.

NRC publishes a direct final rule (91 FR 65091) renewing the AP1000 design certification for 40 years from its effective date and adopting Revision 20 of the design control document; effective 2026-12-28 unless significant adverse comments arrive by 2026-11-13, with a companion proposed rule.

title: Streamline NRC licensing, set review deadlines and replace the ALARA principle
uncertainties: The list of NRC final rules comes from Federal Register API listings (titles and abstracts) read on 2026-10-07; only the fee rule and the categorical exclusions rule were read in part (the first 100,000 characters of each), and the advanced reactor framework, NEPA implementation proposal and generic environmental findings rules were seen as listing abstracts only; the 2026-09-24 licensing, decommissioning and oversight proposal was also not read. The ANS report of 2026-03-13 said the NRC was on target for the 2026-11-23 deadline, while POWER on 2026-05-20 reported the chair conceding delays; the later report is used. The NRC's own count of final rules after May 2026 was not found. Whether any individual licensing review has met the order's 18 month limit was not checked (POWER cites a subsequent license renewal for Robinson finished in under 12 months). Staffing reductions, ACRS changes and commissioner changes were not researched. The 2026-08-21 Federal Register item titled Environmental Protection Regulations is a CFR correction, not a substantive rule. Re-check on 2026-10-15: the three newest NRC items were read as follows: the materials-licensing and AP1000 direct final rules (first 100,000 characters each), the 2026-09-24 proposal as a listing abstract only. Context from the DOE side, not NRC licensing: CRS R48599 (updated 2026-03-25) lists the Office of Nuclear Energy at 1,685.0 million dollars enacted for FY2026 against a 1,370.0 million request (House 1,795.0; Senate bill 1,592.7); the enacting law is believed to be Public Law 119-74, whose Division B covers Energy and Water, but its text on govinfo was truncated and the amount was not confirmed there. POWER Magazine reports DOE's Nuclear Energy Launch Pad, run by the National Reactor Innovation Center, was unveiled 2026-03-04 and named four initial participants on 2026-04-27; it does not replace NRC licensing and the article ties it to Executive Order 14301, not 14300, so it is not counted toward this record. ADVANCE Act implementation and the Part 53 final rule's detailed status beyond the 2026-03-30 framework rule were not separately examined.
